gloss: old rice; rice from a previous harvest

definitions.gloss: old rice; rice held over from a previous year's harvest
definitions.explanation: Rice harvested in an earlier year and stored, as opposed to {新米|しんまい}, the freshly harvested crop. It is still perfectly edible but drier and less fragrant, so it is priced lower and often blended with new rice.

examples.japanese: {古米|こまい}は{少|すこ}し{安|やす}い。
examples.english: Old rice is a little cheaper.

examples.japanese: {古米|こまい}は{水|みず}を{多|おお}めにして{炊|た}くとよい。
examples.english: It's best to cook old rice with a little extra water.

examples.japanese: {新米|しんまい}と{古米|こまい}を{混|ま}ぜて{売|う}っている{店|みせ}もある。
examples.english: Some shops sell new and old rice blended together.

examples.japanese: {古米|こまい}はチャーハンにするとパラパラして、かえっておいしく{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: Old rice comes out nice and loose when made into fried rice, so it actually tastes better that way.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古米|こまい}を{炊|た}く: to cook old rice
- {古米|こまい}と{新米|しんまい}を{混|ま}ぜる: to blend old and new rice
- {古古米|ここまい}: rice two harvests old (the next step down)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新米|しんまい}: newly harvested rice — moist and aromatic, sold at a premium in autumn. Note that {新米|しんまい} also means 'novice, rookie' when applied to a person; {古米|こまい} has no such figurative sense.

USAGE:
Japan's rice year runs from November, so rice from before that changeover becomes {古米|こまい}. The word appears mainly on price tags and in cooking advice rather than in everyday conversation.
